sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles a stretch of the southern Apennines between the Irpinia and Basilicata areas, across the high Sele R. and, S-ward, the high Agri R. valleys, west of the city of Potenza. This source forms the southern core sector of the high-angle, NE-dipping, large normal fault system of the southern Apennines.
Historical and instrumental catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Pondrelli et al., 2006; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show a remarkable destructive seismicity within the area. From north to south, these earthquakes are: 8 September 1694 (Mw 6.9, Irpinia-Basilicata), the well known multiple earthquake of 23 November 1980 (Mw 6.9, Irpinia-Basilicata), 9 April 1853 (Mw 5.9, Irpinia), 19 August 1561 (Mw 6.4, Vallo di Diano -although of uncertain location), 1 February 1826 (Mw 5.7, Basilicata), and the well known multiple earthquake of 16 Dec 1857 (Mw 7.0, Basilicata).
This Source lies at the backbone of the whole NW-SE striking extensional axis of the southern Apennines. The 1980 (to the north) and 1857 (to the south) earthquakes have revealed the occurrence of 25+ km long faults well capable of locally inverting the topography and interfering with drainage. Also, these catastrophic earthquakes have shown mechanisms of normal fault interaction in this region.
The main segments of this Source have been associated with the key earthquakes of the region. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenesis in this region, the reader can refer to the Individual Sources in this Database.
The strike of this Source was based on that of the mapped structures. The dip was based on geological data and geometrical considerations. The rake represents pure extension, based on geological and seismological data. The minimum and maximum depth were based on geological and seismological data. The slip rate was inferred from geological observations in adjacent structures that share the same tectonic environment with this Source.

Epicentral region of the 1857 earthquake also showing location and epicentral intensity of other historical earthquakes (from Benedetti et al. [1998]). The figure also reports the location of the Late-Quaternary Val d'Agri and Vallo di Diano Fault Systems according to Benedetti et al. [1998].

pictures.t: Regional structural section across the southern Apennines
pictures.c: Regional section across the Upper Agri Valley, suggesting also the absence of clearly detectable major normal faults (from Menardi-Noguera and Rea [2000]).

pictures.t: Geological and structural sketch of the high Agri river valley
pictures.c: Geologic sketch showing the main tecto-stratigraphic units forming the shoulders of the Upper Agri River Valley. Bold lines mark Quaternary normal faults responsible for the early stages of the basin opening and for the recent deformation (from Maschio et al. [2005]).

pictures.t: Map of historical and instrumental seismicity of the southern Apennines
pictures.c: Map of historical and instrumental seismicity showing seismic sequenceS that occurred at the boundaries of the main historical earthquake epicentral areas (from Cucci et al. [2004]).
Comparison between the fault model proposed in the DISS database, and the best-fitting solution derived from a seismological analysis performed by Lucente et al. [2005].

pictures.t: Intensities of the 1857 earthquake and R. Mallet route
pictures.c: The map shows the intensities of the 1857 earthquake superposed onto individual seismogenic sources from geological data and the source from intensity data (Boxer method). It shows also the route follewed by R. Mallet (from Burrato and Valensise [2008]).

pictures.t: Mallet's map with epicenter and damage pattern
pictures.c: Map showing the epicenter of the 1857 earthquake as it was calculated by R. Mallet. Note the striking correspondence among the epicenter, the damage distribution and the location of the DISS seismogenic sources (from Burrato and Valensise [2008]).

pictures.t: Felt area of the first shock of the 1857 earthquake
pictures.c: Map showing that the felt area of the strong foreshock of the 1857 earthquake well fit the position of the northern source (from Burrato and Valensise [2008]).

pictures.t: Scheme of ropture sequence of the 1857 earthquake
pictures.c: Scheme of the proposed sequence of rupture for the 1857 earthquake involving the activation of two adjoining sources (from Burrato and Valensise [2008]).
